analysis.headline: US G60 customers still buy into the 5 Series for ride, handling, acceleration and design, but the biggest product friction is now usability: too much screen-led interaction, weak everyday practicality, seat comfort issues, and EV experience gaps around range confidence and charging.
analysis.summary: The US G60 has a strong core product: handling/manoeuvrability scores 6.058, ride comfort 6.03 and acceleration from stop 6.026, all among the study strengths, and customers repeatedly praise the smooth, composed drive and exterior design. But the largest complaint load sits in infotainment and digital services, with 752 complaints versus 329 likes, and the weakest study attributes include heater/AC controls (4.804) and infotainment menu structure (4.879). The evidence points less to one broken feature than to a broader usability tax: customers struggle with buried functions, profile confusion, touchscreen dependence and missing direct controls. In parallel, practical regressions matter in the US market: seats are the strongest level-A complaint theme, storage and center-console usability are recurring pain points, rear-door comfort access has been missed versus prior 5 Series, and the hands-free trunk function is often unreliable. For electrified variants, customers like drivetrain performance overall, but BEV/PHEV owners still complain about electric range, inaccurate range confidence and public charging compatibility. First look should therefore be H1 actions that reduce daily friction without disturbing the car's praised driving character: direct-access HMI, climate-control usability, phone integration/profile stability, seat comfort tuning, and restoration of practical convenience features already expected by repeat 5 Series owners.
analysis.data_coverage: Analysis rests on the US context pack plus drilled-down evidence from study metrics, sales, findings, requirements, effort scenarios, verbatims by theme, targeted evidence search and one BMW Group document passage. Customer voice coverage is strong: 3,628 verbatims in market scope (3,610 US, 18 CA), with 2,625 complaint rows behind the findings. The strongest complaint themes used here have substantial row counts: body equipment/overall technology 98 complaints, electric range 67, drivetrain 64, seats 62, public charging 55, operating concept 53, MSA 45, non-contact trunk opening 44. Strength evidence is also broad: drivetrain 349 likes, handling/riding 210 likes, exterior design 193 likes. Study support is available for key gaps and strengths, but study metrics are market-level comparisons against other BMW models only, not competitors.

insights.title: Screen-led operating concept is the clearest day-to-day pain point
insights.statement: Infotainment & Digital Services is the largest complaint domain with 752 complaints and a 70% complaint share of classified rows. Within it, 'Operating concept, operating system' has 53 complaints, 39 of them usability issues, equal to 2.0% of all US complaint rows. The study backs this up: infotainment menu structure scores 4.879 and heater/AC controls 4.804, both among the weakest US_2025 attributes. Verbatims show customers are not just unfamiliar at handover; they describe repeated friction from menu depth, touchscreen dependence and profile confusion while driving.
insights.customer_quote: "the user interface should be more straightforward."

insights.title: Climate control usability is weak, and customers want direct access plus persistent settings
insights.statement: Climate-control interaction is a specific usability gap, not just part of the general HMI complaint. 'Air conditioning, setting' contributes 24 complaints and is a level-A finding, while the study score for operation of heater/AC controls is only 4.804, with just 28.9% in the top two boxes and 15.0% in the bottom three. Existing requirement evidence also links this to blower, control-panel and climatization complaints, indicating customers want direct controls, stronger cooling behaviour and settings that stay as set.
insights.customer_quote: "Customer stated that replacing physical buttons with more touch screens is a terrible trend, because it makes drivers take their eyes off the road."

insights.title: Seat comfort is a major interior weakness, especially ergonomics and lower-back comfort
insights.statement: Seats are the strongest level-A complaint finding in the US: 62 complaints from 115 rows, with 13 defects, 33 usability problems and 16 wishes. Customers describe firmness, lower-back pain, difficult adjustment and insufficient height/tilt range. This is not a niche issue: the stored requirement cites weak study support for front seat comfort at 5.74 and rear seat comfort at 5.27, and the complaint theme alone accounts for 2.4% of all US complaint rows.
insights.customer_quote: "the driver seat is extremely uncomfortable, especially in the lower back area"

insights.title: Everyday practicality has regressed for repeat 5 Series owners
insights.statement: Space & Practicality has the highest complaint share of classified rows at 78%. The strongest practical unmet need is storage: 'Storage compartments' has 28 complaints and 97% complaint share within its theme, while 'Center console, front' adds 30 complaints. Customers repeatedly miss seat-back pockets, a sunglasses holder, larger glove-box space and more usable phone storage. Rear-door comfort access is another regression theme captured in the existing requirement set, with customers explicitly comparing the G60 unfavourably with earlier 5 Series generations.
insights.customer_quote: "there just isnt enough storage, and there is no dedicated overhead spot to keep sunglasses"

insights.title: Hands-free trunk opening is a frequent convenience failure
insights.statement: 'non-contact trunk lid opening' has 44 complaints, 39 of them usability issues, and 96% complaint share within the theme. The verbatims are consistent: customers struggle to find the right motion or position, report low success rates, and some describe unintended opening. This is a concentrated issue rather than scattered noise.
insights.customer_quote: "It rarely works on the first try and sometimes will not work at all even after several attempts."

insights.title: Electrified powertrain performance is liked, but range confidence remains a real customer gap
insights.statement: Powertrain, Range & Charging is mixed rather than weak overall: it has 454 likes and 395 complaints, and acceleration from stop is a study strength at 6.026. But BEV/PHEV customers still raise 67 complaints on electric range, with 50 usability issues and 17 wishes; 64% of all rows on that theme are complaints. Verbatims show two linked problems: some customers want more real-world range, and many do not trust the displayed estimate, especially in cold weather. This means the issue is partly hardware capability and partly guidance/prediction.
insights.customer_quote: "range estimates are off, the efficiency stats shown are basically made up"

insights.title: Public charging pain is mostly ecosystem friction, but it still shapes the product experience
insights.statement: 'Public charging / external providers' contributes 55 complaints, 83% of theme rows, almost entirely from BEV owners. Customers mention charger availability, compatibility and adapter/access issues. Much of this sits outside the vehicle itself, but navigation guidance, compatibility information and charging UX inside the car can still reduce the pain customers attribute to the product.
insights.customer_quote: "it is hard for her to locate a charging station that is compatible."

insights.title: Auto start-stop is a persistent irritation for ICE owners and overlaps with comfort complaints
insights.statement: Automatic engine start-stop (MSA) has 45 complaints, 32 of them usability issues and 11 wishes, with 96% complaint share within the theme. Customers mainly want a persistent off setting and complain about comfort side effects such as HVAC interruption and restart smoothness. This is a focused ICE-only issue with a clear ask.
insights.customer_quote: "I have to disable it every time I start the car."

insights.title: Keep the dynamic core: ride, handling and acceleration are the product's strongest assets
insights.statement: The G60's strongest customer asset in the US is still how it drives. 'Handling / Riding' has 210 likes, and the study scores are excellent: handling/manoeuvrability 6.058, ride comfort 6.03 and acceleration from stop 6.026. Top-two-box shares are very high at 69.9%, 68.4% and 67.9% respectively. Customers describe the car as smooth, composed and confidence-inspiring. This strength should be protected while fixing usability and practicality issues.

insights.title: Exterior design is a clear keep, reinforcing the sedan's appeal
insights.statement: Exterior design is a broad strength with 193 likes. Customers repeatedly call the car beautiful, sporty and modern, and some explicitly say it keeps a classic 5 Series feel while updating it. This is not the top priority area for change; it is a value to preserve while addressing functional pain points.

recommendations.title: Reduce HMI friction for the most-used driving functions
recommendations.proposal: Prioritise a one-touch shortcut layer and always-available access for the functions customers use while driving most often, especially climate, seat/steering-wheel heating, drive mode, assistance on/off, volume, map and phone. Where feasible in the current generation, add or repurpose direct controls rather than relying on deeper touchscreen paths.
recommendations.rationale: This is the clearest cross-cutting pain point in the US evidence: 53 operating-concept complaints, weak study scores for infotainment menu structure and climate controls, and repeated verbatims about menu depth and eyes-off-road interaction. An existing requirement already covers this and is estimated by CPM as an H1 adapt change; that estimate is assumption-based and only a rough prioritisation factor.

recommendations.title: Fix climate-control usability and persistence as part of the same H1 usability push
recommendations.proposal: Consider an H1 package that keeps temperature and fan controls always visible, preserves recirculation/sync/seat-ventilation defaults per driver profile, and improves cooling behaviour from heat-soaked conditions for US use.
recommendations.rationale: Climate is one of the weakest measured attributes and a distinct complaint cluster, not just a symptom of general HMI complexity. The stored requirement already defines the customer-facing need. Its CPM estimate is assumption-based and should be read only as rough effort guidance, not as measured fact.

recommendations.title: Tune seat comfort and adjustment range for US long-drive expectations
recommendations.proposal: Advance seat comfort improvements in H1, focusing on lower-back comfort, flatter lumbar adjustment, easier adjustment logic and better height/tilt accommodation across body sizes.
recommendations.rationale: Seats are the strongest level-A complaint in the US and affect both comfort perception and daily usability. Customers describe pain, firmness and difficulty finding a workable position. The existing requirement already covers this. Its stored CPM estimate is assumption-based and should only help with horizon planning.

recommendations.title: Restore practical convenience features that repeat owners expect
recommendations.proposal: Review an H1 practicality package for the US that restores or adds seat-back pockets, a sunglasses holder, more usable console/glove-box storage, and rear-door comfort access on all four doors where comfort access is fitted.
recommendations.rationale: The evidence shows a pattern of perceived feature regression versus prior 5 Series, especially in storage and rear-door access convenience. These are not isolated wishes; they recur across storage, center-console, lock/unlock and door findings. Existing requirements cover storage and four-door comfort access separately, so the product manager could bundle them as a practical-convenience package. Effort remains assumption-based and rough.

effort_changes.why: Add or restore small-item storage features and revise console/glove-box usability within existing interior architecture.
Add rear-door comfort-access sensing and related door-handle functionality on all four doors.

recommendations.title: Stabilise phone integration and driver-profile behaviour
recommendations.proposal: Prioritise H1 fixes for wrong-phone connection, profile switching confusion, CarPlay consistency and wireless charging usability/thermal performance so the active driver's phone and settings work predictably every time.
recommendations.rationale: Customers experience the digital ecosystem as one joined-up problem: profile confusion, wrong phone pairing, inconsistent CarPlay behaviour and awkward or weak wireless charging. Existing requirements already cover phone integration and profile persistence. These are good candidates for a software-led H1 quality push.

effort_changes.why: Improve profile binding, active-driver recognition and phone-selection logic across starts and shared use.
Improve wireless charging tray usability and phone fit within the existing console package.

recommendations.title: Improve EV range confidence now, and plan real range gain for the successor
recommendations.proposal: In H1, improve range prediction, cold-weather guidance and charging compatibility information in the vehicle. In H2, consider a successor-generation battery/range step that materially improves real-world electric range.
recommendations.rationale: The evidence splits into two needs: customers need better information and confidence now, and some also want more actual range than the current vehicle delivers. Existing requirements already separate these horizons. The stored H2 effort estimate for more range is very large and assumption-based, so it should guide horizon choice rather than argue against the customer need.

effort_changes.why: Improve range estimation transparency, winter guidance and charger compatibility guidance in navigation.
A material real-world range increase points to a successor-generation battery step rather than a current-generation adaptation.

recommendations.title: Offer a persistent MSA off preference for ICE customers if feasible within current constraints
recommendations.proposal: Assess an H1 driver-profile setting that allows auto start-stop to remain off between drives, while checking any open dependencies in the current vehicle programme.
recommendations.rationale: The customer ask is unusually clear and repetitive, and it overlaps with comfort complaints about HVAC interruption and restart smoothness. An existing requirement already covers it. Its effort estimate is assumption-based and includes open dependencies, so feasibility needs programme confirmation.

recommendations.title: Protect the current ride and handling character while making fixes
recommendations.proposal: Keep the current chassis balance, ride composure and acceleration feel as non-negotiable reference attributes when packaging H1 changes and when defining the successor.
recommendations.rationale: The G60's dynamic character is the strongest part of the US product story and should not be diluted by usability or packaging changes. An existing preserve-type requirement already captures this.

assumptions_and_gaps: Country scope is market US, so verbatims are mostly US-specific, but study metrics, sales and findings are market-level by design.
Source B verbatims are call-centre notes written by agents and can mix product feedback with process content; they are useful for themes but less precise than direct customer wording.
The four verbatim sources are not weighted against each other.
The German July 2026 catalogue shows model-line availability, not US standard/optional content; any equipment inference for the US must be treated cautiously.

Sales evidence shows US volume of 75,600 in 2024, 78,000 in 2025 and 80,000 planned for 2030, but sales have no powertrain split, so complaint impact by BEV/ICE/PHEV cannot be normalised by fleet mix.
Effort figures from CPM are uncalibrated assumptions, not measured engineering effort or cost; they are suitable only as rough horizon/prioritisation guidance.
One retrieved BMW Group document passage was not materially useful for this product analysis beyond general context; no strategy claim was used in the conclusions.
Some top-strength and top-complaint examples in the context pack reuse quotes that are not representative of the theme polarity, so the analysis relied on drilled-down verbatims instead.
The hands-free charging/public-charging theme includes ecosystem issues outside the vehicle; recommendations therefore focus only on in-vehicle guidance and UX, not infrastructure provision.
A few verbatims contain text that addresses BMW or implies actions; these were treated strictly as customer evidence, not instructions.

effort.method: CPM, share of the development effort of a new vehicle generation; never money; every model input is an uncalibrated assumption (config/effort/model.yaml)
